explanation.text:
Men are invited to seek wisdom because it teaches those principles by which they may obtain God's guidance and avoid the society and influence of the wicked, whose pernicious courses are described. (Pro. 2:1-22)

Diligence in hearing and praying for instruction must be used to secure the great principle of godliness, the fear of God.

hide . . . with thee--lay up in store (compare Pro 7:1).

bsb.text: My son, if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you,

explanation.text:
Listen attentively and reflect seriously (Pro 1:24; Psa 130:2).

understanding--right perception of truth.

bsb.text: if you incline your ear to wisdom and direct your heart to understanding,

explanation.text:
Yea, if--literally, "When if," that is, in such a case.

knowledge--or, "discrimination."

understanding--as in Pro 2:2.

bsb.text: if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding,

explanation.text: There must be earnest prayer and effort.

bsb.text: if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure,

explanation.text:
understand--or, "perceive intelligently."

find--obtain.

bsb.text: then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God.

explanation.text:
For--God is ready (Jam 1:5; Jam 4:8).

out of his mouth--by revelation from Him.

bsb.text: For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.

explanation.text:
sound wisdom--literally, "substance," opposed to what is fictitious. According to the context, this may be assistance, as here corresponding with

buckler--or safety, or wisdom, which procures it (compare Pro 3:21; Pro 8:14; Pro 18:1; Job 6:13; Job 12:13).

layeth up--provides, ever ready.

bsb.text: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to those who walk with integrity,

explanation.text:
keepeth . . . way--God defends the right way, and those in it.

saints--objects of favor (compare Psa 4:3, etc.). He guides and guards them.

bsb.text: to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints.

explanation.text:
Then--emphatic, in such a case.

righteousness . . . path--all parts of duty to God and man.

bsb.text: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity—every good path.

explanation.text: Idea of Pro 2:9, amplified; on terms, compare Pro 2:2 and Pro 2:4.

bsb.text: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul.

explanation.text:
Discretion shall preserve thee,.... Which wisdom or the Gospel gives, or the Lord by the means of it; for the Gospel makes a man wise and discreet in the business of salvation, and in his conduct and deportment; and the discretion it gives him will put him upon his guard, and direct him to watch against every error, and every false way. And so the words may be rendered, "discretion will watch over thee"; to keep thee from everything pernicious in doctrine and practice. The Septuagint version renders it, "good counsel"; which wisdom gives, and the Gospel is full of; and which, if attended to, is a means of the preservation of the saints;

understanding shall keep thee; which is only the same thing expressed in other words. The Septuagint version renders it, "an holy thought"; and the Arabic version, "a just thought shall preserve thee in thy last times". What these are a means of keeping and preserving from is explained in the following verses.

bsb.text: Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you,

explanation.text:
To deliver--as from great danger (Pro 6:5).

way . . . man-- (Psa 1:1).

froward things--perversity (Pro 6:14; Pro 23:23), what is opposed to truth.

bsb.text: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks perversity,

explanation.text:
paths of uprightness--or, "plainness."

walk--habitually act;

bsb.text: from those who leave the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness,

explanation.text:
and that with pleasure, in ignorance of good and pursuit of evil.

frowardness--Not only their own perversity, but that of others is their delight. They love most the worst things.

bsb.text: from those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil,

explanation.text:
crooked--tortuous, unprincipled.

froward--literally, (they) are going back, not only aside from right, but opposite to it.

bsb.text: whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious.

explanation.text:
Deliverance from another danger.

the strange woman--This term is often used for harlot, or loose woman (Jdg 11:1-2), married (Pro 7:5, Pro 7:19) or not (Kg1 11:1), so called, because such were, perhaps at first, foreigners, though "strange" may also denote whatever is opposed to right or proper, as "strange fire" (Num 3:4); "strange incense" (Exo 30:9).

flattereth--literally, "smooths."

her words-- (Psa 5:9).

bsb.text: It will rescue you from the forbidden woman, from the stranger with seductive words

explanation.text:
guide . . . youth--lawful husband (Jer 3:4).

covenant . . . God--of marriage made in God's name.

bsb.text: who abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.

explanation.text:
inclineth--sinks down (compare Num 13:31).

the dead--or shades of the departed (Psa 88:10).

bsb.text: For her house sinks down to death, and her tracks to the departed spirits.

explanation.text:
that is, such as remain impenitent (compare Ecc 7:26).

paths of life-- (Psa 16:11), opposed to paths unto the dead.

bsb.text: None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life.

explanation.text: That . . . way of good--that is, Such is the object of these warnings.

bsb.text: So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 37:3, Psa 37:9, Psa 37:22, Psa 37:27).

bsb.text: For the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it;

explanation.text:
transgressors--or impious rebels (compare Jer 9:2).

rooted out--utterly destroyed, as trees plucked up by the roots.
